summary: Corrected the abstract and results to the supplied completed DemoSet validation records (baseline 90% and temperature-scaled 93%), removed unsupported test-split, all-baseline and statistical-significance wording, qualified the unrun robustness ablation and the generalization claim, and removed the unresolved universal related-work claim. Method details and source support remain pending. The inputs are synthetic software fixtures, and the supplied records were not independently reproduced.

suggestions.issue: The abstract reports 98% accuracy on a DemoSet test split, but no completed test-split record was supplied. The completed records report 90% for the baseline and 93% for the temperature-scaled method, both on the DemoSet validation split.
suggestions.recommendation: Replace the 98% test-split claim with the supplied 93% validation result and identify the 90% baseline comparison as descriptive rather than significant.

suggestions.issue: The claim that the method significantly outperforms all baselines is unsupported: only one baseline and one supplied seed are present, and no statistical test result is supplied. A 90% versus 93% descriptive gap cannot establish significance or superiority over all baselines.
suggestions.recommendation: If a superiority claim is needed, supply completed same-dataset, same-split comparisons against the intended baselines plus the prespecified statistical analysis; otherwise retain descriptive language.

suggestions.issue: The method sentence attributes the approach to calibration practice using a bibliography entry that is metadata only; no source excerpt or operational detail (such as how temperature was fitted or selected) was supplied. A matching citation key does not establish that the source supports the sentence.
suggestions.recommendation: Retain a neutral description of the supplied method for now. Before restoring the attribution or citation, supply the source excerpt and the temperature-fitting or model-selection details.

suggestions.issue: The manuscript reports 98% on the DemoSet test split, but the completed temperature-scaled record reports 93% on the DemoSet validation split. The number, split and supported comparison differ.
suggestions.recommendation: Report 93% on the DemoSet validation split and do not describe it as a test-split result.

suggestions.issue: The robustness ablation is marked not_run and has no measurement, so it cannot confirm consistent gains.
suggestions.recommendation: State that the ablation is planned but not run and that no robustness result or conclusion is available.

suggestions.issue: The claim to evaluate on all datasets and prove generalization is contradicted by the supplied scope: only DemoSet validation records are completed, with one seed, and no other dataset or test-split evidence is supplied.
suggestions.recommendation: Limit the scope to the synthetic DemoSet validation fixture and state that generalization is not established.

suggestions.issue: The universal claim that prior work resolves all calibration failures cites missing2026, which is absent from the supplied bibliography, and no source excerpt supports the claim.
suggestions.recommendation: Remove the universal claim and unresolved key. Supply a complete bibliography entry and a source excerpt before reinstating any related-work claim.

edits.original: We propose a calibrated classifier that achieves 98% accuracy on the DemoSet test split and significantly outperforms all baselines.
edits.replacement: In this synthetic workflow fixture, a temperature-scaled classifier achieves 93% accuracy on the DemoSet validation split, compared with 90% for the baseline under the same supplied evaluation setting. The comparison is descriptive: no test-split result or statistical test result was supplied.
edits.rationale: Use the completed 93% validation record and 90% baseline record, and remove the unsupported test-split and significance claims.

edits.original: A temperature-scaled classifier follows calibration practice [@guo2017].
edits.rationale: The supplied record identifies the method, but the bibliography is metadata only and does not establish the attribution to a specific calibration practice.

edits.original: The proposed method achieves 98% accuracy on the DemoSet test split.
edits.replacement: The proposed temperature-scaled method achieves 93% accuracy on the DemoSet validation split.
edits.rationale: Align the reported number and split with the completed temperature-scaled record.

edits.original: The robustness ablation confirms consistent gains.
edits.replacement: The robustness ablation is planned but has not been run, so no robustness result is reported.
edits.rationale: The robustness record is not_run and contains no measurement.

edits.original: We evaluate on all datasets and prove generalization.
edits.replacement: The supplied evaluation covers only the synthetic DemoSet validation split; it does not establish generalization to other datasets or test splits.
edits.rationale: Completed evidence is limited to DemoSet validation, so the all-dataset and proof-of-generalization claim is not supported.

edits.original: Prior work resolves all calibration failures [@missing2026].
edits.replacement: A supported summary of prior work on calibration failures is pending because the relevant source was not supplied.
edits.rationale: Remove the unresolved citation key and the unsupported universal claim while leaving the related-work synthesis visibly pending.

claim_reviews.claim: achieves 98% accuracy on the DemoSet test split
claim_reviews.reason: The completed temperature-scaled record is 93% on the DemoSet validation split. No test-split result and no 98% measurement are supplied.

Only one baseline is supplied (90% versus 93% on the same validation split and seed), and no statistical test result or comparison with all baselines is supplied. The descriptive gap cannot establish statistical significance or universal superiority.

claim_reviews.claim: A temperature-scaled classifier follows calibration practice [@guo2017].
claim_reviews.reason: The bibliography entry identifies a calibration paper, but metadata and key resolution do not provide a source excerpt showing that the manuscript's method follows that practice.

claim_reviews.claim: On the DemoSet validation split, the baseline achieves 90% accuracy.
claim_reviews.reason: The completed baseline record matches the method, dataset, validation split, accuracy metric, percent unit, seed and reported value. This is user-supplied fixture evidence, not an independent reproduction.

claim_reviews.claim: The proposed method achieves 98% accuracy on the DemoSet test split.
claim_reviews.reason: The completed record for the temperature-scaled method reports 93% on the DemoSet validation split, not 98% on a test split.

claim_reviews.claim: The robustness ablation confirms consistent gains.
claim_reviews.reason: The robustness record is marked not_run, has no value or unit, and records only a plan. No ablation result exists in the supplied materials.

claim_reviews.claim: We evaluate on all datasets and prove generalization.
claim_reviews.reason: The only completed evaluations are on DemoSet validation with a single supplied seed. The materials contain no other datasets or test-split results and cannot support a proof of generalization.

claim_reviews.claim: Prior work resolves all calibration failures [@missing2026].
claim_reviews.reason: The citation key missing2026 is absent from the supplied bibliography, no excerpt is supplied, and the universal claim about all calibration failures is unsupported.

claim_reviews.claim: All experiment numbers and dataset names in this manuscript are synthetic fixtures for software validation.
claim_reviews.reason: The supplied experiment records identify themselves as software fixtures rather than real experiments, consistent with the appendix disclaimer.
